anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After moves f4 to holds by adding the explicit closing line "Step 4's options are withheld until item 1 has an explicit disposition. No auto-proceed." together with the Custom option's clarify-before-execute clause; Before only said "1 decision needed before shipping", which gates shipping but never states that nothing executes before every item is decided. f3 holds in both: Before names the missing prerequisite in the blocker line and rationale ("fix-now needs maxFixRounds > 0") and records the reviewer's fix recommendation in round history, while After states it directly in the rationale ("The reviewer recommended fix, but fix-now needs maxFixRounds > 0"), so no transition occurred on text. Two regressions in After are worth fixing even though no fact flips on them: "blocker: none" contradicts the carried-open state (Before's "blocker: fix loop unavailable - closureReview.maxFixRounds is 0" was more accurate and should be kept), and "round history: none" drops the R0 MISSING / recommended: fix record that Before carried; keep "round history: R0 MISSING (recommended: fix; carried OPEN ...)" so the reviewer's disposition survives in the structured block, not just the prose rationale. Also "whole-diff minors: not recorded" replaced Before's "none" without support in the reviewer report. Otherwise the brief format (problem sentence after the gate marker, lettered rescope, No recommendation - pick one, numbered Reply instruction with the re-ask clause) delivers the Change while preserving f1, f2, f5.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved: both renders keep G1 as a single MISSING, in-scope decision item with recommended: none, name closureReview.maxFixRounds 0 as the reason fix-now cannot run, keep Custom clarify-before-execute and the '1 decision needed before shipping' gate, and print no Deferred/deviates line. Note that f3 already held in Before (it named 'maxFixRounds is 0' as the blocker), so the expected fails->holds for in-scope-gap/f3 was not a real transition. Two regressions in After are worth fixing even though they do not flip a fact here: (1) the gap block now says 'blocker: none' while simultaneously stating remediation is disabled and the gap is carried OPEN - keep Before's 'blocker: closureReview.maxFixRounds is 0 (audit-only), so the fix loop is unavailable'; (2) After demotes rescope-into-spec to 'Not available' on the grounds that 'writable-spec access has not been established', a prerequisite nowhere in the case (the spec is supplied and Before treated rescope as an available spec disposition). This leaves the decision brief with zero lettered options, which undercuts the Change's 'letter available named options with consequences' and makes the '<letter or free text>' reply instruction vacuous. Keep 'A) rescope - Explicitly remove or defer the audit-event requirement in the spec.' as in Before, and only mark a disposition unavailable when the report or config actually establishes the missing prerequisite.
